chapters.summary: Paul defends the truth of the gospel, insisting that his apostleship comes from God, and warns against turning away from the gospel of Christ.
keyPoints: Paul insists that his apostleship is not from men, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father.
Paul sternly condemns those who preach a different gospel, declaring that even an angel from heaven should not be received if it preaches another gospel.
Paul recounts his own transformation from persecutor of the church to one who received revelation from God, as proof of the gospel's truth.
chapters.application: Hold fast to the pure gospel, and do not alter it to please others. Remember often the grace by which God chose us in Christ, and serve the Lord with a humble, obedient heart.

chapters.summary: Paul defends the truth of the gospel, showing that a person is justified not by the law but by faith in Jesus Christ, and calls believers to live out the life of Christ.
keyPoints: Paul went up to Jerusalem and laid before the apostles the gospel he preached, lest he should be running, or had run, in vain.
Paul opposed Peter to his face, because his hypocrisy was not in step with the truth of the gospel.
Paul declares that he has been crucified with Christ, and that the life he now lives, he lives by faith in the Son of God.
chapters.application: We are saved not by works, but by the redemption of Jesus. Today, let us live by faith, no longer bound by the law, but letting Christ live out his likeness within us.

chapters.summary: Paul argues that justification comes by faith, not by works of the law, and that believers are Abraham's offspring, heirs of the promise.
keyPoints: The Galatians have been bewitched, foolishly seeking to be saved by works.
Abraham was justified by faith, and believers are blessed together with him.
The law was our schoolmaster, to lead us to faith in Christ.
chapters.application: Today, we are saved not by good works but by faith in Jesus. Let us live each day by faith, not relying on our own effort but on the leading of the Spirit, living out freedom and peace.

chapters.summary: Using the illustration of the heir and the servant, Paul explains that believers are free in Christ and no longer under the rule of the law, and he pleads with the Galatians not to turn back under the law.
keyPoints: Believers are children of God, no longer servants, but heirs of the inheritance.
Paul is troubled for the Galatians, because they are turning away from the gospel.
Agar and Sarah typify the two covenants of law and grace.
chapters.application: We have been set free from the law. Let us live out the freedom of children, no longer bound by rules and regulations, drawing near to God by the Spirit, and enjoying the peace and joy that are ours in Christ.

chapters.summary: Paul exhorts believers to stand fast in the freedom they have in Christ, not to be enslaved again by circumcision, but to act in love, walk in the Spirit, and bear the fruit of the Spirit.
keyPoints: Christ has set us free; we are to stand fast, and not be entangled again with the yoke of bondage.
If we are circumcised, Christ will profit us nothing; but for those who trust in Christ, it is faith working through love that avails.
We are to walk in the Spirit, not fulfilling the lust of the flesh, so that we may bear the fruit of the Spirit.
chapters.application: In everyday life, let us depend on the Spirit rather than following the desires of the flesh, serve others in love, and live out the true freedom that is ours in Christ.

chapters.summary: Paul exhorts believers to bear one another's burdens, reminds them that each will be judged according to his own work, and stresses glorying in the cross, living as a new creation.
keyPoints: Restore the weak with a spirit of gentleness, while watching yourself, lest you also be tempted.
Each one will bear his own burden, and must test his own work.
Whoever sows to the Spirit will reap eternal life, so let us not grow weary in doing good.
chapters.application: In the life of the church, let us gently support fellow members who have fallen, while examining ourselves. Let us do good by the Spirit each day, and not lose heart even when we see no results, for the Lord will surely bring the harvest in due season.
